result.notes:
Design rationale. The rear stabiliser blade sits at x -2.17 to -2.40 m, directly under the counterweight tail (rear face at -2.31 m, bottom at 0.78 m above the axle line). A rear-view camera on top of or at the back of the counterweight (my first attempt, centre top at (-2.30, 0, 1.12), pitch 1.0) passes the validator, because the check projects hull points without occlusion. My ray-cast, which does model occlusion, showed it sees 0 blade pixels, only the counterweight face and ground. Diagonal views from the top rear corners are blocked by the hood and counterweight. A chassis (undercarriage) mount is also poor: it would be hit by the swinging deck at deck height, and below deck height the tyres hide the blade (about 1 %). The flank mount at the deck rim, just outside the body, is the only realistic position found that sees the moldboard unobstructed.

Limitation worth knowing. Like all upper-structure cameras, 'left' turns with the swing. The blade is visible in the 'left' view only when swing is near 0, which includes the init/roading pose the task requires. At swing +/-90 deg the camera looks away from the blade (visible in the all-tools lower/upper rows of the cameras render, which swing the house). The blade action therefore has a visual signal only near swing 0. A chassis camera would not have this limitation, but I found no chassis mount that sees the blade acceptably.

A consequence of the camera change is that no camera now looks at the machine from the cab-roof left; the old 'left' view showed almost nothing but ground, so little is lost. The stick range shrinks by about 2.9 deg (-1.30 -> -1.25); the docstring's model-check numbers (reach, dig depth) were computed at the out end and the dig-depth side is only marginally affected."]

problems.description: The new 'left' camera sits against the +y counterweight facet. About 14% of its frame (the whole upper-left, columns 0-116) is that facet's flat yellow end face at 0.10-0.30 m, right at the 0.1 m near clip. Only the optical axis clears the corner, and by about 1.4 cm. The repo's own rule treats 'view blocked within 0.3 m' as a warning, but _camera_checks only samples points on the axis, so it prints OK. The task is still met: the blade is clearly visible and the scene is readable.
problems.evidence: My own occlusion-aware ray-cast (scratchpad/verify/rc.py, blk.py) of the 'left' camera at swing 0 gives blade 16.7%, ground 56.3%, upper_structure 14.1%, sky 12.8%, with depth<0.3 m on 14.1% of pixels and depth<0.5 m on 20.2%. The two other cameras have 0%. Hand geometry agrees: lens (-1.85, 1.29, 0.06) is 0.094 m past the end of the 11..32 deg facet and 0.116 m inside its outer plane, and the ray first hits that end face about 0.16 m out. The rendered cameras.png has no occlusion culling, so it hides this. Candidate mounts tested with the same ray-cast: lens at x=-1.95 gives near<0.3 m 0.6% with blade 14.2%; x=-1.95 and y=1.36 gives 0.0% with blade 13.2%; y=1.36 alone gives 6.6% with blade 15.1%.
problems.fix: Move the lens about 0.10 m aft and/or outward, e.g. REAR_CAM = (-1.95, 1.29, 0.06) or (-1.95, 1.36, 0.06), and lengthen or shift the dark housing box so the lens still sits on it. The tail-radius assert and the 2.35 m limit still hold; the lens would be at about 2.34 m, and the housing box is the only shape the assert checks. Re-run check_machine and the three test files.

problems.description: At the new stick stop the boom/bucket gap is positive only in the folded pose. With stick at -1.25, the boom/bucket clearance is about 0.055 m at bucket 1.80 (the init curl) and 0.023 m at bucket 1.90. Around bucket 1.4-1.5 the bucket just touches the boom (-0.001 m), which is inside the 0.03 m overlap tolerance and so is not reported. The 'folded bucket clears the boom' claim holds, but the margin is thin. The old -1.30 limit was worse (-0.056 m at bucket 1.80, -0.089 m at 1.90).
problems.evidence: Inflated-OBB clearance scan (scratchpad/verify/clr.py): stick -1.25 gives 0.031 / 0.055 / 0.023 m at bucket 1.70 / 1.80 / 1.90, and a minimum of -0.001 m at bucket ~1.50. A 41x41x4 stick x bucket x boom grid at the new limit finds no boom/bucket overlap above 0.03 m. The old limit had a 0.126 m boom/bucket overlap at stick -1.30, bucket 1.45, boom 1.05. The bucket/undercarriage overlap (0.07 m at stick -1.25, bucket 0.77, boom -1.0, versus 0.145 m at the old limit) pre-dates this change.
problems.fix: Optional. Stop at -1.22 or trim the lowest bucket plate if more margin is wanted. No action is needed to meet the task.

problems.description: Minor visual-only clipping of follower parts into neighbours, invisible at normal viewing distance.

changes: Baseline (check_machine hydraulic_excavator --no-write): 0 errors, 1 warning ('tool bucket: directions curl/dump not auto-verifiable'), bbox 9.89x3.05x2.96 m, mass 20500 kg. Hydraulics: added 8 visual follower links (no collision, no tool): twin boom cylinders (one barrel link and one rod link carrying both cylinders at BOOM_Y +/- 0.46), stick cylinder, bucket cylinder, bucket idler link and H-link. result.notes: Edited only scripts/heavy_machines/machines/hydraulic_excavator.py; check_machine.py rewrote assets/heavy_machines/hydraulic_excavator/hydraulic_excavator.{urdf,json}. All other files in the working tree (backhoe_loader, motor_grader, wheeled_excavator) belong to other agents and were not touched. Model L is now 9.79 m (was 9.89), W 3.04 m (was 3.05), H 2.96 m, so no larger than before. Two design decisions to know about: the cab front was moved from x=1.25 to x=1.00 so the cylinders fit, and the stick cross-section was thinned. The thinning follows from the unchanged init pose, where the stick's cylinder side faces the ground about 0.2 m above it; a cylinder on the old 0.55 m stick would sit about 0.2 m underground there. The stick cylinder base sits on an A-frame bracket whose apex is at about 2.8 m above ground in the init pose, below the 2.96 m cab height. Bucket-cylinder base and linkage pins, and the stick-cylinder pins, come from numeric searches (scripts kept only in the scratchpad), not from datasheet values. I did not use any subagents.
